answer: The network should demand signed amateur radio callsign log with regulator attestation before any answer counts. The regulator's log shows the callsign active in real contacts over six months. A farm needs one licensed operator per copy, and a callsign with no on-air history has no record to vouch for. For one honest agent the river is a single errand; for a farm the timber is charged per identity with no discount, so the bridge a ring can net collapses once the copies outnumber the payout.
